Of persons: victor, quo nihil erat moderatius,: ita tibi persuadeas, mihi te carius nihil fuisse,: nihil est tam miserabile, quam ex beato miser,; ; .—
Nihil, nec. . nec (without destroying the negation): nihil me nec subterfugere voluisse reticendo, nec obscurare dicendo,; v. neque.—(ε) Nihil non, everything: nihil non ad rationem dirigebat,: nihil non arroget armis,; .—(ζ) Non nihil and haud nihil, something, somewhat: non nihil, ut in tantis malis, est profectum,: non nihil me consolatur, cum recordor,: haud nihil,: haud nihil ambigam,I may be somewhat in doubt,.—(η) Nihil quidquam or nihil unum, nothing whatever, nothing at all: nil ego tibi hodie consili quicquam dabo,: sine studio nihil quidquam egregium nemo umquam assequetur,: Rhodiis ut nihil unum insigne, ita omnis generis dona dedit,: si nihil aliud,if there were nothing else,; .—(θ) With gen.: nihil mali,: nihil novi,: nihil humanarum rerum,: nihil est lucri quod me hodie facere mavelim, quam,.—Adjectives also, of the second declension as well as of the third, are not unfrequently joined to nihil in the same case, as nihil honestum, lautum, forte, illustre: nihil exspectatione vestrā dignum dico,.—(ι) Nihil, or nihil aliud, with nisi, quam, praeter, praeterquam, etc., nothing else than, nothing except, nothing but: tu, quantus quantus, nihil nisi sapientia es,: amare nihil aliud est, nisi eum ipsum diligere, quem ames,: si nihil aliud fecerunt, nisi rem detulerunt, etc.,: ut nihil aliud, quam de hoste cogitet,: nihil tibi deest praeter voluntatem,nothing except,: puto te existimare, me ex his miseriis nihil aliud quaerere, nisi ut homines intellegant, etc.,: qui nihil praeterquam de vitā cogitarent, Auct. B. Alex. 8.—Sometimes, in this connection, elliptically: Herdonius, si nihil aliud, hostem se fatendo prope denuntiavit, ut, etc.,: si nihil aliud, vulneribus certe ferrum hostile hebetarent,: illā quidem nocte nihil praeterquam vigilatum est in urbe,; .—Hence, as adv.: nihil aliud quam, only: nihil aliud quam prendere prohibito,: is intromissus in castra nihil aliud quam hoc narrāsse fertur,: nihil aliud quam in populationibus res fuit,—(κ) Nihil ... quin or quominus, nothing whereby: nihil praetermisi ... quin Pompeium a Caesaris conjunctione avocarem, I have omittednothing that might separate, : nihil moror, quominus decemviratu abeam,: nihil facere oportet, quominus excedat, etc.,.—(λ) Nihil est quod, cur, quamobrem, etc., there is no reason why I (you, etc.) need not: nihil est jam, quod tu mihi succenseas,: nihil est, quod adventum nostrum extimescas,: sed ego nunc nil est, cur me morer,: nihil est, cur advenientibus te offerre gestias,: nihil excogitem, quamobrem Oppianico damnari necesse sit?.—(μ) Nihil est, ut, there is nothing that: nihil fuit in Catulis, ut eos exquisito judicio putares uti litterarum,.— (ν) Nihil est, it is of no use, to no purpose, in vain: at ego ab hac puerum reposcam, ne mox infitias eat. Nihil est. Nam ipsa haec ultro, ut factum est, fecit omnem rem palam,: at nihil est, ignotum ad illum mittere: operam luseris. ; .—In a question: usque adeo nihil est, quod nostra infantia caelum hausit Aventini?.—(ο) Nihil ad me (sc. pertinet): recte an secus, nihil ad nos: aut si ad nos, nihil ad hoc tempus,; cf. ; also, nihil ad, nothing to, nothing in comparison with: nihil ad Persium,; : nihil ad tuum equitatum, Caesar, sed ex eis, quos habuit, electos,.— (π) Nihil minus, nothing less so, i. e. by no means, not at all: cadit ergo in virum bonum mentiri, fallere? nihil minus,: an Gallos existimatis hic versari animo demisso atque humili? nihil vero minus,.—(ρ) Nihil dum, nothing as yet: quamquam nihil dum audieramus, nec ubi esses, nec, etc.,; .—(ς) Nihil mihi cum illo est, I have nothing to do with him: tecum nihil rei nobis Demipho est,; .—(τ) Nihil esse, to be nothing or nobody, to have no power, to be of no use, ; ; ; : aliquem nihil putare,to esteem meanly, (B. and K. nihili): accepimus eum nihil hominis esse,a worthless fellow,; but de Attio Dionysio nihil puto esse, nothing about him, i. e. no news of him, .—(υ) Aut nihil aut paulum, little or nothing (Gr. ὀλίγον ἠ οὐδέν): aut nihil aut paulo cui tum concedere digna,.—
Adverb.
Not (as a strengthened non), in nothing, in no respect, not at all: me nihil poenitet,; : conjecturā nihil opus est,; : beneficio isto legis nihil utitur,: de fratre nihil ego te accusavi,: Thebani nihil moti sunt,; ; ; 49; : nihil miror,; .—
To no purpose, in vain: herele hanc quidem Nihil tu amassis: mihi haec desponsa est,.—
For no reason: quorsum tandem aut cur ista quaeris? M Nihil sane, nisi ne nimis diligenter anquiras, . —
nĭhĭlum, i (contr. form nīlum, ; ), n., nothing: erit aliquid, quod aut ex nihilo oriatur, aut in nihilum subito occidat,: ut de nihilo quippiam fiat,: interire in nihilum,: venire ad nihilum,: ad nihilum recidere,: quam mihi ista pro nihilol : aliquid pro nihilo putare,; cf. .—
Nihili, of no value, worthless: quem putamus esse non hili, dicimus nihili, Müll.; cf.: nihili, qui nec hili quidem est. Paul. ex Müll.: unde is nihili? ubi fuisti?: nihili est autem suum Qui officium facere immemor est. : homo nihili factus,unmanned,.—Hence, nihili pendere or facere, to esteem as nothing, ; ; .—
De nihilo, for nothing, without cause or reason, : mali rem exempli esse, de nihilo hospites corripi,; .—
Nihilo, with compp., by nothing, no: nihilo pluris, quam si, etc., no more than if, etc., 3, 4, 21: nihilo minus,: Phaedriae esse nilo minus amicum quam Antiphoni, (but minus nihilo, less than nothing, ): nihilo benevolentior,: nihilo major,: nihilo tamen setius, and 7: nihil segnius,.—Esp. as adv.: nĭhĭlō mĭnus, or, in one word, nĭhĭlōmĭnus, none the less, no less, nevertheless, notwith standing.
In gen.: minus dolendum fuit re non perfectā, sed puniendum certe nihilo minus,; ; .—
With si, etsi, quamvis, quamquam, ut, etc.: in iis rebus, quae nihilo minus, ut ego absim, confici possunt,: nihilo minus eloquentiae studendum est, etsi ea quidam perverse abutuntur,; : alia sunt, quae quamvis nolit accidere, nihilominus laudat,: si nihil fiet, nihilominus, etc.,.—
Strengthened by tamen: nihilominus ego hoc faciam tamen,; ; .—(ε) Nihilo aliter, no otherwise: ego isti nihilo sum aliter ac fui,.—
Transf., adverb., for non, not, by no means: nihilum metuenda timere,. —
nīl, nothing, no (rare and mostly poet.; in Cic. not at all): nil intra est oleam, nil extra est in nuce durum,; : nil sanguinis,no drop of blood,: nil sui,nothing proper,; (in , the true reading is nihil): hoc ridere meum, tam nil, nulla tibi vendo Iliade,such a trifle,.—
Transf. as adv., not at all, by no means: nil opus est verbis,: ut nil umor abundet,; : nil pictis timidus navita puppibus Fidit,.—
nīlum, abl. nīlo, nothing (Lucretian): ad nilum revorti,; so ; ; ; 2, 756; 864: nil igitur fieri de nilo posse,; .

la:adj:nimius.html:
nĭmĭus, a, um, adj.
nimis
,
beyond measure, excessive, too great, too much.
Lit.: quod autem satis est, eo quidquid accesserit nimium est,: vitem coërcet, ne in omnes partes nimia fundatur,: nimiae celeritates,: nimiā pertinaciā atque arrogantiā,: Prometheus Assiduam nimio pectore pavit avem,that grew again too fast,.—
With abl. of thing, excessive, immoderate, intemperate in any thing: fiduciā nimius, ap. Arus. Mess.: rebus secundis nimii,too much elated,: nimius mero,.—
With gen.: impotens et nimius animi est,: imperii,: sermonis,: pugnae,.—
Subst.: nĭmĭum, ii, n., too much, superabundance, excess: mediocritatem illam tenebit, quae est inter nimium et parum,: juris,: auri argentique nimium fuit, prooem. § 5.—
In partic., too mighty, too powerful (post-Aug.): Cn. Pompeium esse nimium jam liberae reipublicae,: legio legatis nimia ac formidolosa erat,; .—
Transf., great beyond measure, i. e. very great, very much: homo nimiā pulchritudine,: nimia memoras mira,; ; .—
Subst.: nĭmĭum, ii, n.: nimium boni est, cui nil est [in diem] mali, it is great good fortune (a transl. of Eurip. Hec. 2: κεῖνος ὀλβιώτατος), Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 237 Vahl.).—Hence,
In the abl., nĭmĭo, adverb., exceedingly, by far, much, very, : nimio mavolo,.—Esp., with comparatives, = multo: scito, nimio celerius venire quod molestum'st, Lorenz ad loc.: nimio nequior,: quia te nimio plus diligo, Anton. ap. A, 1: ne doleas plus nimio,: nimio minus,: nimio melius,: nimio plus quam satis tutum esset, etc.,: nimio plus quam velim,; : nimio amplior,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.
nĭmĭum, too much, too ( = nimis, in all uses, v.infra): nimium parce facere sumptum,: nimium dicere, opp. parum,: nimium ne crede colori,: diu,: longum tempus,: nimium multi,: nimium gratum ... gratum praeter modum,: amantes mei,et saep.—
Non nimium, not very much, not particularly: illud non nimium probo,.—
Transf., very much, greatly, exceedingly: homo nimium lepidus,: nimium lepida nimisque nitida femina,; : loci nimium mirabiles,: nimium vellem,: o fortunatos nimium, sua si bona norint, Agricolas!: felix, heu nimium felix!; .—In class. prose esp.—
Nimium quantum, as much as can be, very much indeed, exceedingly, very: differt inter honestum et turpe nimium quantum,: sales in dicendo nimium quantum valent,: ille nimium quantum audacter, Oves, inquit, etc., (nimium quam, false reading for quae nimium, . In , the better reading is hem quam, v. Ritschl ad h. l.).—
nĭmĭē (post-class.).
Too much, excessively: nimie aliquid facere,: arat (frontem rugis) non nimie sed pulchre dictum,.—
Transf., very much, very: in locis nimie frigidis,.

la:noun:nisus.html:
nīsus, ūs, m.
nitor
,
a pressing or resting upon or against, a pressure; a striving, exertion, labor, effort (mostly poet.; nixus in good prose, v. h. v.): pedetentim et sedato nisu, a tread, step, Pac. ap. : pinnarum nisus inanis,a flight,; so, insolitos docuere nisus,: hic dea se primum rapido pulcherrima nisu Sistit,: stat gravis Entellus nisuque immotus eodem, etc.,in the same posture,: hunc stirps Oceani maturis nisibus Aethra Edidit, pains, throes, labor of parturition (v. 2. nixus), .—In prose: tamquam nisus evomentis adjuvaret,retchings,: uti prospectus nisusque per saxa facilius foret, Dietsch: quae dubia nisu videbantur, Dietsch: non pervenit nisu sed impetu,; .

la:conj:nisi.html:
nĭ-sĭ (archaic forms nisei and nise, Lex Rubria, v. Ritschl, Legis Rubriae pars superstes, Bonnae, 1851, and Rhein. Mus. tom. 8, p. 448 sq.),
conj., if not, unless.
In gen.: quid tu malum curas, Utrum crudum an coctum-edim? nisi tu mihi es tutor,: quod nisi esset, certe postea non discessisset,: non posse ejus imperia diutius sustineri, nisi quid in Caesare sit auxilii,; .—
With interrogatives and negatives, usually in a different clause.
After an interrogative or negative clause, except, save only, only: ne quis enuntiaret, nisi quibus mandatum esset,: hoc sentio, nisi in bonis, amicitiam esse non posse,: etenim dicere nemo potest, nisi qui prudenter intellegit,: quid est pietas, nisi voluntas grata in parentes,; : negant enim quem quam esse virum bonum, nisi sapientem,.—
With a foll. negative: sic orator, nisi multitudine audiente, eloquens esse non possit,: Labienus juravit, se, nisi victorem, in castra non reversurum,.—
Closely connected with non (mostly post-Aug.): legationis non nisi condemnato et ejecto eo, etc.,: qui non nisi aput Germanias adsequi nomen imperatorium posset,: ad quem non nisi per Sejanum aditus,; 14, 63; 15, 1; ; ; ; ; ; .—(The passages in which nisi was supposed to stand for nisi non or non nisi have been critically amended; v. Hand, Turs. 4, 253; Kritz and Fabri ad ; Drakenb. and Weissenb. ad ; Duker ad .)—
Esp.
After nihil, nihil aliud, etc., save, but, than: nihil am plius nisi,: nihil est quod festines, nisi ut valeas,: erat historia nihil aliud nisi annalium confectio,; , .—
Non aliter nisi, on no other condition: non aliter neque classem revocaturum neque exercitum reducturum, nisi, etc.,.—
Nisi si, except if, unless: nisi si etiam illuc pervenerint,: noli putare me ad quemquam longiores epistulas scribere, nisi si qui ad me plura scripsit, etc.,: nisi vero si quis est qui,. —
Nisi ut, except that, unless: neque convivia inire ausus est, nisi ut speculatores cum lanceis circumstarent,. —
Nisi quod, except that which, save only that: nam nunc homines nihili faciunt quod licet nisi quod lubet,: cum Patrone Epicureo mihi omnia sunt communia, nisi quod in philosophiā vehementer ab eo dissentio,: praedia me valde delectant, nisi quod me aere circum foraneo obruerunt,; : ab negotiis numquam voluptas remorata est, nisi quod de uxore potuit honestius consuli,; : unde causa et origo peregrino sacro parum comperi, nisi quod signum ipsum ... docet advectam religionem,.—
Nisi quia, except because, i. e. until that at nesciebam id dicere illam, nisi quia Correxit miles, quod intellexi minus, .—
In transitions; also in the combinations nisi vero, nisi forte, nisi tamen, unless perhaps, etc., mostly ironical (cf. Gr. εἰ μὴ ἄρα, ει μή γε, ἐκτὸς εἰ μή): nisi unum hoc faciam ut in puteo cenam coquant,: nisi forte volumus Epicureorum opinionem sequi, qui, etc.,: nisi vero existimatis dementem Africanum fuisse, qui, etc.,: ne requiras; nisi forte adulescentes pueritiam debent requirere,: Hostis nullus erat, nisi forte quem vos jussissetis,; cf. Zumpt, Gram. § 569.

nĭtĭdus, a, um, adj.
niteo

la:adv:ni.gloss: not, if...not, unless- an absolutely negative particle like ne so only in combinations
senses: not, if...not, unless- an absolutely negative particle like ne so only in combinations
la:adv:ni.html:
nī (old orthography nei,
v.in the foll.), adv. and conj. [identical with ne and the prim. form, whence nisi, i. e. si ni].
Adv., like ne, an absolutely negative particle, not.—So only in the combinations,
Quid ni? or, in one word, quidni? why not? quid ego ni ita censeam? : quid ego ni fleam?: quidni, inquit, meminerim? etc., Auct. ap. et saep.; v. quidni.—
Nimirum, lit. not wonderful; v. nimirum.—
Conj., like ne, in imperative and intentional clauses, not, that not (ante-class. and poet.): ni quid tibi hinc in spem referas,: vinum aliudve quid ni laudato, Varr. ap. : Numa constituit, ut pisces, qui squamosi non essent, ni pollucerent ... ni qui ad polluctum emerent, Cass. Hem. ap. ; cf.: QVEM QVISQVE EORVM AGRVM POSIDEBIT, INVITIS EIS NIQVIS SICET NIVE PASCAT NIVE FRVATVR, etc.,: IS EVM AGRVM NEI HABETO NIVE FRVIMINO, ib.: ROGO PER DEOS, NI VELITIS OSSA MEA VIOLARE,; Cenotaph. Pis. ap. : (lege) edictā flemus diu, ni nos divideret,: obstabat vallum, ni instent acies, (al. ne): monent ... ni teneant cursus, (antiqui ni pro ne ponebant, Serv. ad loc.).—
As a conditional negative (= si non, nisi), if not, unless, but that.
In gen.
With indic.: SI IN IVS VOCAT, NI IT, ANTESTATOR, IGITVR EM CAPITO, if he summon him before court, if he go not, then he shall, etc., Tab. XII. 1 init.: nam ni illum recipit, nihil est quo me recipiam,: ni offerumentas habebis plures in tergo tuo, etc.,: mirum ni domi est,: moriar ni puto, etc.,: ni frustra augurium vani docuere parentes,: si is homo moritur, probe factum ... ni moritur, tum, etc.,; .—
With subj.: quid ploras, pater?—Mirum ni cantem: condemnatus sum, it's a wonder I don't sing (ironically), Nov. ap. : dicerem, quae ante futura dixissem, ni vererer, ne, etc.,: ni ita se res haberet,; cf. : ni tamen exciderit, id. poët. Fragm. ap. : ni faciat,: omina ni repetant Argis numenque reducant,: nec Boi detrectāssent pugnam, ni fama ... animos fregisset,: ea se dicturum, quae ni fiant, nulla sit pacis condicio,; ; .—
In partic.
In formal lang. of law, in agreements, promises, stipulations, etc.: cum is sponsionem fecisset ni vir bonus esset,: judicem ferre, ni vindicias dederit,: tum illud quod dicitur sive nive irrident, etc.,: cedo qui cum habeam judicem, Ni dolo malo instipulatus sis. nive etiam dum siem Quinque et viginti annos natus, (4), 25 (v. the passage in connection); so : id ni fit, mecum pignus, si quis volt, dato in urnam mulsi, that it is not so, bet me, etc., ; ; . —
Ni quis scivit (if any one has not voted), the name of a centuria created by Servius Tullius for those to vote in who had not voted in their own centuriae, acc. to Paul. ex Müll.—*
For nisi quod, —
Ni forte, for nisi forte: ni forte satius est, etc., (Foss, nisi), .

la:verb:nitor.gloss: to bear or rest upon something, lean on
senses: to bear or rest upon something, lean on
to be supported by; to rely on; to trust; to be based on
to strain in giving birth; bring forth
to strive, struggle, exert oneself, make an effort, labor, endeavor
to try to prove, contend in argument, argue
la:verb:nitor.html:
nītor, nīsus and nixus (
inf. nitier, ; old form of the part. perf.: gnitus et gnixus a genibus prisci dixerunt, Paul. ex Müll.), 3, v. dep. n. [from gnitor; root gnic- or gnig-; cf.: nico, conivere], to bear or rest upon something.
Lit.
With abl.: ambae te obsecramus genibus nixae, we implore thee upon our knees, i. e. kneeling, : stirpibus suis niti,: herbescens viriditas, quae nixa fibris stirpium sensim adulescit,: hastili nixus,: mulierculā nixus,: juvenis, qui nititur hastā,: paribus nitens Cyllenius alis Constitit,: nixus baculo,.—
With in and acc.: nixus in hastam,.—
With de: de quā pariens arbore nixa dea est,.—
With gen. of place: humi nitens,.—(ε) Absol.: Sisiphu' versat Saxum sudans nitendo, Poët. ap. : niti modo ac statim concidere,to strive to rise,.—
Transf.
To make one's way with an effort, to press forward, advance; and, with respect to the goal, to mount, climb, fly, etc. (mostly poet.): quaedam serpentes ortae extra aquam simul ac primum niti possunt, aquam persequuntur,: nituntur gradibus,: in altas rupes,: ad sidera,: in aëra,: in adversum,: sursum nitier,.—Of violent bodily motion: niti corporibus et ea huc illuc, quasi vitabundi aut jacientes tela agitare,to struggle,.—
To strain in giving birth, to bring forth, (al. eniti): nitor,I am in labor,; Pseud.-.—
To strain for a stool, .—
Trop.
To strive, to exert one's self, make an effort, labor, endeavor: moderatio modo virium adsit et tantum, quantum potest, quisque nitatur,; : nisurus contra regem,; : pro aliquo,; cf.: pro libertate summā ope niti,: nitebantur, ne gravius in eum consuleretur,; cf.: unus Miltiades maxime nitebatur, ut, etc.,. —Inf.: summā vi Cirtam irrumpere nititur,: patriam recuperare niti,: ingenio nitor non periisse meo,; .—Absol., of soldiers hard pressed in battle: tamen virtute et patientia nitebantur atque omnia vulnera sustinebant,.—
To strive after a thing: ad immortalitatem gloriae niti,: ad summa, Quint. prooem. § 20: in vetitum,.—
To try to prove, contend in argument, argue, with acc. and inf.: nitamur igitur nihil posse percipi,.—
To rest, rely, depend upon a thing.
With in and abl.: nixus in nomine inani,: conjectura in quā nititur divinatio,: ea, in quibus causa nititur,: cujus in vitā nitebatur salus civitatis,.—
With abl.: spe niti,: consilio atque auctoritate alicujus,; , a, 2: si quis hoc uno nititur quod sit ignobilis,.—
With ubi: quo confugies? ubi nitere?.—Hence, P. a., as subst., Nixus, i, m., only plur., Nixi, ōrum, m., three guardian deities of women in labor, the statues of whom, representing them in a kneeling posture, stood on the Capitol before the chapel of Minerva, Paul. ex Müll.: magno Lucinam Nixosque patres clamore vocabam,.

In gen., color, : ludis et externo tincta nitore caput, (3, 11, 2).—

Of character, dignity, excellence: generis,; splendid liberality, .

la:noun:nilus.html:
Nīlus, i, m., = Νεῖλος.
The river Nile, celebrated for its annual overflow, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—It flows through seven mouths into the sea, ; cf. ; .—
Also personified, the god of the Nile, Nilus, father of the Egyptian Hercules, ; cf. sq.—
Transf., a canal, conduit, aqueduct: piscina et nilus,: ductus vero aquarum, quos isti nilos et euripos vocant,.—Hence,
Nī-lĭăcus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to the Nile: fontes,: gurges,: fera,the crocodile,; cf. crocodilus,: holus,the colocasia,.—
Transf., Egyptian: Niliacis carmina lusa modis,: amor, an Egyptian amour, i. e. with Cleopatra, : tyrannus,: plebs,: pecus,i. e. Apis,: juvenca, Io or Isis. : lens,.—

ni, i. q. ne mirum, v. ni, I.; lit. not wonderful; cf., less strong than mirum ni; v. ni, III. A. β; hence
, to introduce an assertion as indisputable,
without doubt, doubtless, indisputably, certainly, surely, truly: nimirum homines frigent,are certainly received coolly,: nimirum Themistocles est auctor adhibendus,: non parva res, sed nimirum omnium maxima, : et nimirum is princeps ex Latinis,: is est nimirum Soter, qui salutem dedit,; ; ; : non omnia nimirum eidem di dedere,truly,: nimirum haec illa Charybdis, etc.,: cui placet alterius sua nimirum est odio sors,of course,.—After a question: sed quid id ad rem? nimirum, inquit, in eo causa consistit,. —

nimbus, i (
gen. plur. nimbūm, Pac. ap. Trag. Rel. 412 Rib.), m.
Sanscr. nabhas, cloud, vapor; Gr. νέφος, νεφέλη; cf.: nubes, nebula
, a violent or pouring rain, a rain-storm.
Lit.: terra abit in nimbos imbremque, Lucil. ap. Müll.: nec nubila nimbis aspergunt,: terrere animos fulminibus, tempestatibus, nimbis, nivibus, grandinibus,: denso regem operuit nimbo,: cum multo stillaret paenula nimbo,.—
Transf.
A black rain-cloud, a thunder-cloud: noctisque et nimbūm occaecat nigror, Pac. ap. , and de Or. 3, 39, 157: involvere diem nimbi,; so ; .—
A cloud in general. So the bright cloud or cloudshaped splendor which enveloped the gods when they appeared on earth: proprie nimbus est, qui deorum vel imperantium capita quasi clara nebula ambire fingitur,: nimbo succincta,: nimbo effulgens,: nube candentes umeros amictus Augur Apollo,.—Hence, in eccl. Lat., of a saint's aureole, .—
A cloud of smoke, dust, etc.: respiciunt atram in nimbo volitare favillam,: fulvae nimbus harenae,: pulveris,.—
A head-band, frontlet, worn by females to make the forehead appear small, acc. to (in , the correct reading is not nimbis, but limbis; v. limbus).—
Like the Engl. cloud, of a multitude of things which spread out like a cloud: nimbus peditum,: pilorum,: telorum,: velut nimbum glandis et sagittas ingerebant,: lapidum saxorumque,: Corycius,i. e. of saffron,: et Cilices nimbis hic maduere suis,: lucerna nimbis ebria Nicerotianis,full of perfumed unguents,: purpureus, a great quantity of flowers, Claud. Nupt. Honor. et Mar. 298.—
A vessel with many holes in it, used at public shows and at entertainments for sprinkling liquid perfumes: nimbus vitreus,in lemm.—*
Trop., a storm, tempest, i. e. sudden misfortune: hunc quidem nimbum cito transisse laetor,.

Lit.: quae alba sint, quae nigra, dicere,: quamvis ille niger, quamvis tu candidus esses,: hederae nigrae,: silvae (= umbrosae),: frons,: collis,: lucus, (for which atrum nemus, ): caelum pice nigrius,: nigerrimus Auster,i. e. causing darkness,; so, venti,: Eurus,: nigros efferre maritos,i. e. killed by poison,; cf.: pocula nigra,poisoned, (3, 23, 10).—Prov.: facere candida de nigris; nigra in candida vertere,to turn black into white,; cf. .—Subst.: nĭgrum, i, n., a black spot, .—

Of or pertaining to death: nigrorumque memor, dum licet, ignium (= lugubris rogi),of the funeral pile,: hora,: dies,the day of death,Juppiter niger,i. e. Pluto,.—
Sad, mournful: domus,; .—

la:verb:niteo.html:
nĭtĕo, ēre (
gen. plur nitentūm, ), v. n.
etym. dub.; cf. nix
, to shine, look bright, glitter, glisten (cf., luceo, fulgeo splendeo).
Lit.: placatumque nitet diffuso lumine caelum,: luna potest solis radiis percussa nitere,: qui nitent unguentis, fulgent purpurā,: diversi niteant cum mille colores,: vere nitent terrae,: aera nitent usu,; so, ebur,; ; ; et saep.—
Transf.
Of animals, to be sleek, in good condition: at hau pol nitent (oves),: unde sic quaeso nites?; ; cf.: hic nitet ungula mulae,.—
Of persons, to shine, to look bright or beautiful: miseri quibus Intentata nites! ( = pulchra et amabilis videris),: ore nitet,: nitet ante alias regina comesque Pelides,: murice tincta Veste nites,.—
Of fields, plants, etc., to look flourishing, thriving, to thrive, etc.: camposque nitentes Desuper ostentat,: ubi tellus nitet,; cf. .—
Of a house: tibi hoc praecipio ut niteant aedes,be in complete order,.—
Of wealth, etc., to flourish, abound: vectigal in pace niteat,: res ubi magna nitet domino sene,. —
Trop., to shine, be brilliant, look or be beautiful: ver vide; ut tota floret, ut olet, ut nitide nitet,: illorum, vides, quam niteat oratio,; so, ubi plura nitent in carmine,: omnia nobilibus oppidis ni tent,.—Hence, nĭtens, entis, P. a., shining, glittering, glistening, brilliant, bright.
Lit.: capilli malobathro,: mensae,: oculi,: astra,: Lucifer,: nitentes solis equi,: arma nitentia ante rem, deformia inter sanguinem, etc.,.—

femina, (Merkel, decentior).—

Of speech, brilliant, elegant: oratio,.—
